title: useWorkspaceAdminStatus grants workspace-admin UI from a NAME in positions[], which #15948 made tenant-writable
body:
`useWorkspaceAdminStatus` decides workspace adminship from three legs, and the third one scans the
session's `positions[]` array for an admin-sounding **name**:

```ts
// packages/auth/src/useWorkspaceAdminStatus.ts:119-121
const isAdmin =
  isAdminRole(activeMember?.role) ||
  isAdminRole(user?.role) ||
  (Array.isArray(positions) && positions.some(isAdminRole));
```

`ADMIN_ROLES` contains `platform_admin` (alongside `owner`, `admin`, `super_admin`, `superadmin`,
`system_admin`). So `positions` containing the string `platform_admin` makes this hook answer
`isAdmin: true`.

## Why that is now a defect and was not obviously one before

Framework `8e0b29758` — `fix(plugin-auth)!: session payload positions[] is the security axis, not
the better-auth role scalar` (objectstack#15948, landed 2026-09-05, a declared BREAKING change) —
changed what that array **is**. It used to be the `sys_user.role` scalar split on commas. It is now
built by `resolveUserAuthzGrants` and carries ADR-0057 D4 `sys_user_position` assignments.

`sys_user_position` is `apiEnabled` and its `position` values are unconstrained. The framework's own
changeset for the companion fix states the consequence plainly:

> a tenant could mint a row spelling `platform_admin` for one of their own users:
> `resolveUserAuthzGrants` pushed that name straight onto `grants.positions`, while `grants.posture`
> — derived from the unscoped `admin_full_access` grant and nothing else — correctly stayed
> `MEMBER`. Every reader of the name therefore answered `true` for a principal enforcement treats as
> an ordinary member.

The framework treated this as a real defect and fixed **four** server-side sites
(`plugin-sharing`, `plugin-approvals`, `plugin-security`, `runtime`), each now testing
`posture === 'PLATFORM_ADMIN'` instead of the name. `resolve-authz-context.ts` states the rule at
`hasPlatformAdminStanding`: *"read the RUNG — never `positions.includes(...)`"*.

This client site is the same defect on the other side of the wire, and it was not in that sweep.

## Severity — stated honestly

**This is not privilege escalation.** The server was fixed; `platform-admin-gate.ts` dropped its
positions leg and `isPlatformAdmin` derives from the posture rung, so API calls from such a
principal are still refused. What a tenant gets by minting the row is a **Console that paints
platform-administrator surfaces at one of their own users** — nav entries, marketplace access,
whatever else `useWorkspaceAdminStatus` gates — while every underlying call fails.

That is worth fixing on two grounds: it is misleading in the direction that reveals platform
structure to a tenant-controlled account, and it is the exact pattern the framework just banned by
name. Rating it p2 rather than p0 for that reason; re-rate if any consumer of this hook does
something more load-bearing than showing UI.

## Why the obvious fix is wrong, and what the real one has to preserve

⛔ Do not simply delete the third leg. Its docblock explains why it exists:

> This is the ONLY leg that sees a platform administrator whose adminship comes from the
> `admin_full_access` permission set: on a single-tenant deployment there is no member row to read
> (leg 1), and the server deliberately no longer overwrites `user.role` (leg 2), so `positions`
> carrying `platform_admin` is the whole signal.

Deleting it blinds the Console to real platform administrators — that is objectui#5389 regressed.

The replacement signal is `user.isPlatformAdmin`. The docblock currently argues **against** reading
it:

> not alongside the derived `user.isPlatformAdmin` either — that flag is computed by the server as
> `'platform_admin' in positions` from the same expression, so reading both would be two spellings
> for one fact

**That reasoning is now obsolete and it is the crux of this card.** After #15948 they are no longer
one expression: `isPlatformAdmin` is derived from the posture rung (the unscoped
`admin_full_access` grant), while `positions` is a tenant-writable array. They can now disagree, and
when they do, the rung is right. The comment must be rewritten, not just the code — a future reader
who finds the old justification will re-introduce the scan.

Note also that `org_owner` / `org_admin` in `positions` are a separate question from
`platform_admin`: a tenant minting those names is claiming authority **within their own tenant**,
which is not the same exposure. Decide each name deliberately rather than swapping the whole set.

## Acceptance

- a session whose `positions` contains a tenant-minted `platform_admin`, with no
  `admin_full_access` grant, does **not** get `isAdmin: true`
- a genuine platform administrator on a single-tenant deployment (no member row, `user.role` not
  overwritten) still **does** — the objectui#5389 case, still pinned by
  `__tests__/workspaceAdminPositions-5389.test.tsx`
- the `isResolved` semantics from objectui#5619 are unchanged

## How this was found

Not from a report — from a sweep. Framework #15948 arrived in cloud via a pin bump
(objectstack-ai/cloud#2038) and the accompanying warning about `positions.includes('platform_admin')`
prompted checking every consumer of the payload. `objectstack-ai/cloud` came back clean (zero
gate-style reads of `positions`, counter-checked); the framework had already fixed its own four;
this is the one live site the sweep found.
